A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf C$ be a [[Definition:Locally Small Category|locally small category]], $F: \mathbf C^{\text {op} } \to \mathbf {Set}$ a [[Definition:Functor|functor]] and $A$ an object.
Then [[Definition:Natural Transformation|natural transformations]] $\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {-, A} \Rightarrow F$ correspond bijectively to elements of $\map F A$, via $\alpha \mapsto \map {\alpha_A} {\operatorname {id}_A}$.
In particular the [[Definition:Yoneda Embedding|Yoneda embedding]] is [[Definition:Fully Faithful Functor|fully faithful]].

B_source.statement:
Let $G$ be a [[Definition:Group|group]].
Then $g \mapsto \paren {x \mapsto g x}$ embeds $G$ in the group of permutations of $G$, and the permutations commuting with all right multiplications are exactly the left multiplications.

derived.commuting permutations are left multipli: natural transformations are determined by one element

object_map.reformulation: Generalize the regular representation from a one-object category to an arbitrary category: an equivariant map out of a representable is determined by the image of the identity.

validity_conditions: Local smallness makes Hom(-, A) a functor into Set.
For a one-object category, the lemma recovers Cayley's theorem.
proof_plan:
Let $\alpha: \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {-, A} \Rightarrow F$ and $u = \map {\alpha_A} {\operatorname {id}_A}$.
For $f: B \to A$, naturality gives:
:$\map {\alpha_B} f = \map {\alpha_B} {\operatorname {id}_A \circ f} = \map {\map F f} {\map {\alpha_A} {\operatorname {id}_A} } = \map {\map F f} u$
so $\alpha$ is determined by $u$.

Conversely, for $u \in \map F A$, $\map {\alpha^u_B} f = \map {\map F f} u$ is natural by functoriality of $F$, and $\map {\alpha^u_A} {\operatorname {id}_A} = u$.
Hence the correspondence is bijective.

Taking $F = \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {-, A'}$ gives $\map {\operatorname {Nat} } {\map {\operatorname {Hom} } {-, A}, \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {-, A'} } \cong \map {\operatorname {Hom} } {A, A'}$, so the Yoneda embedding is fully faithful.

For a group regarded as a one-object category, natural self-maps of $G$ acting on itself are left multiplications, and the embedding is [[Cayley's Theorem (Group Theory)|Cayley's theorem]].
{{qed}}
